title: Google's open-source Docsy documentation project is moving to the Linux Foundation, with new features aimed at AI agents.
key_facts: Docsy, a Google-created documentation theme for the Hugo site generator, is moving to the Linux Foundation.
The move was announced in a keynote at Open Source Summit Europe in Prague.
By the end of 2024 about 2,200 projects used Docsy, including Kubernetes, OpenTelemetry, gRPC and Jaeger.
Since version 0.15.0, Docsy can produce a Markdown copy of each page and an llms.txt index for AI tools; both are opt-in.
Version 0.17.0 adds a hidden directive that points visiting agents to llms.txt; that feature is also experimental.
quote_evidence: Docsy, the Google-created documentation project used by major cloud native projects, is now moving to the Linux Foundation as it adds features aimed specifically at that machine audience.
Both features are opt-in and remain experimental.
why_it_matters_hint: Better-organised documentation can answer routine questions before they reach maintainers, and it can help AI tools use a project correctly.
